paragraphs: The High Elf Queen was clearly leveraging the power of players to advance her own agenda—and that, more than anything, was becoming a dangerous problem.
"Surely Queen Yvaeris is overwhelmingly powerful," Leon said quietly, his tone thoughtful. "I mean, who in all of Yunatea could actually stand against her right now?"
He paused, his mind turning through the possibilities.
"Humans no longer have a Divine Champion. The Demons... their Ancestral Divine Champion is sealed in Hell. And as for the Dragons..."
Another pause.
"Ivana has only just awakened to her true role. I'm not convinced she's ready to match Queen Yvaeris—not yet."
Freya leaned back, her voice soft but firm. "You're forgetting the Dwarves. And the Giants."
"I don't know much about the Ancestral Divine Champions of either of those races," Leon admitted.

Freya nodded slowly. "That's not surprising. According to the old legends, they were the least involved in the great war that once raged between the High Elves, Demons, and Dragons. They stayed in the shadows—or simply chose not to intervene."
She hesitated a moment, then added, "If we're talking about raw, overall power... the Ancestral Divine Champion from Human, King Elandorr, could have stood against Queen Yvaeris."
"But King Elandorr is no longer in Yunatea," Leon replied. "He passed his responsibilities on to me."
He exhaled, rubbing a hand down his face as the weight of everything began to settle on his shoulders.

This wasn't just another political shift or minor faction war. This was escalating—fast. Now, even the Ancestral Divine Champions were beginning to move again. And that meant the stakes had never been higher.

"Queen Yvaeris has the power to apply absolute rules to anyone in her presence," Leon continued. "She can force entire armies to drop their weapons. Or render people powerless with a single command. That kind of ability... it's insane."
"No matter how strong her enemies might be," he went on, "if she can simply rewrite the rules of battle to make them weaker—then how is she supposed to be stopped?"
They sat in silence for a moment, the weight of the conversation settling between them like a thick fog. Then, with a sudden glint in her eyes, Freya spoke again.
"Or... I've got an interesting idea for you."
Leon turned toward her slowly, immediately suspicious. Her mischievous expression confirmed his instincts. "I never trust your ideas," he said flatly.
Freya nudged his side with her elbow, smirking. "Just hear me out. If Queen Yvaeris is really sending players across the North Continent to hunt down Ivana, then why not... kill the players?"
Leon chuckled, baring a grin. "That's exactly what I was thinking.

He paused, thoughtful now. "But they'll probably have their respawn points set on the continent. Even if I wipe them out, they'll just come back. And there won't be just a few of them—there'll be hundreds, even more."

His eyes narrowed, a new edge forming in his tone. "And there's no way I can use my Broken identity for this kind of massacre. It's too public. Too risky. No... I'll use my Demon form. That'll be far more fun anyway. I haven't had many chances to fight as it."

Freya nodded. "Makes sense. Their numbers will be overwhelming—and a lot of them are Divine Champions. Most of the ones you've seen in the Eternal Challenge? Yeah, expect to meet them again out there."
Leon ran a hand through his hair. "Then this just got a whole lot more interesting. Because it means I'll be facing them in Yunatea."
With that, he stood, stretching out his arms and rolling his shoulders as if shaking off the last of the stillness.
"I'm heading out. I'll think this over some more later."
The journey had been long, and though their time at sea offered little more than the chance to hunt oceanic monsters, it was enough to keep the ship's crew from falling behind in level.
Now, after finally passing beyond the waters bordering the Central Continent, the reinforcements they'd been expecting began to make their appearance.

Broken stood on the deck of the ship alongside the others, the cold wind tugging at their cloaks as they stared out over the vast, rolling sea. The waves ahead of them surged, rising unnaturally high—and beneath those towering swells, shadows moved. Massive, deliberate. Like ancient titans swimming in silence.
Then they saw them.
Gigantic armored whales breached the surface. On their broad, plated bodies stood soldiers—silent figures clad in the distinctive armor of Queen Nerisa's elite force.

The soldiers made no sound. No signal. They merely revealed themselves in formation, a quiet message of presence, power, and control. And then, just as silently as they had come, the armored whales descended once more, vanishing into the deep.

The sea stretching between the Central and North Continents was a different beast altogether. The air here was frigid, sharp enough to sting the lungs, a constant reminder of the icy realms ahead. The North Continent itself was cloaked in snow for most of the year, and even its bordering waters carried that same biting chill.
According to Ronan, this particular part of the ocean was especially wild. Dangerous in ways even seasoned sailors found unsettling.
That was why they hadn't taken the usual route.

Instead of crossing via the common passage—an area patrolled by Central Continent forces and tightly monitored by High Elf Queen's naval scouts—they'd opted for a broader, riskier route. One that looped wide through the less-traveled edges of the sea. It was slower, colder, and far more treacherous... but it offered one vital advantage
They were moving under the radar. And for this mission, that was everything.

With their reinforcements now in place, the crew gathered in the central chamber of the ship to review their next steps. The cold sea winds were behind them, and the distant landmass of the North Continent loomed closer by the days.
Mizuki stood at the center of the room. Everyone leaned in as she began her briefing.

"We'll make landfall here," she said, pointing to a remote section along the continent's icy coastline. "It's far from any major settlements. There aren't many people in the area, and it's well away from the main roads. That means fewer eyes on us—and fewer complications."
She glanced around at the group, her expression serious. "But we need to consider something important: should we set our respawn points at the nearest city... or not?"
Her eyes drifted toward Broken, waiting for his opinion.
Broken had already been thinking about that very issue. He stepped forward, folding his arms as he looked over the map.
"If I die, I can return to Vensalor Island instantly," he said. "And from there, I can use the gate to come right back to the ship—assuming Aego remains stationed in the North Continent."
He paused, then added, "The same applies to all of you. If you end up back at Vensalor Island, you can still return to this ship through the exit gate."
But then his tone shifted, more thoughtful now. "However, if we all die at once—if every crew member respawns at the island—then we'd have a problem."
The room fell into a contemplative silence.

"In that scenario," Broken continued, "Aego would have to be recalled back to the island. There's no way we can leave the ship anchored out here, in hostile territory, without anyone aboard. It'd be far too risky."

He leaned over the map again, eyes narrowed. "We need to plan for that worst-case situation. Because the moment we set foot on the North Continent, we're not just walking into the unknown—we're stepping into enemy territory."

Broken looked around the room, his gaze passing over each member of the crew. It was clear from their expressions—some of them were already thinking the same thing he was. But it made sense for the idea to come from him. It always did.

"All right," he said, his voice steady. "Once we make landfall on the North Continent, I'll separate from the group. I'll head to the nearest city—or wherever I can find the most efficient respawn point based on distance and accessibility. That way, if anything happens, I won't be kicked all the way back to Vensalor Island. We can't risk having to make that entire sea journey again from scratch."
The others nodded in agreement. The logic was sound.

"This will also give me better mobility," Broken continued. "I'll be able to move independently, stay low-profile. With the right disguise, no one will recognize me. No eyes, no suspicions. So yeah... we go with this plan."
Everyone agreed without hesitation. The decision was made, and the course was clear.
The journey continued. Day after day, the icy winds and dark waters stretched endlessly ahead. Until finally, after several weeks at sea, the silhouette of land began to emerge on the horizon.
The North Continent.

The entire crew gathered on the ship's deck, silent as they stared toward the distant shore. Jagged trees lined the coastline—enormous, twisted things that towered far beyond the size of any forest Broken had seen before.
There was something ancient about the land. Something untouched. Something watching.
Just what kind of journey awaited them here?

chapters.title: Chapter 902 902 - Single Horned Player
paragraphs: "Is everyone here?" asked a man with short blond hair and a towering, muscular frame. His voice cut clearly through the crisp northern air.
Beside him, a woman with long, flowing blonde hair gave a brief nod. "Yeah, I think we're all set," she replied. That was ScarletDusk.

Hollow—one of the Envy Champions—stood at the head of the group. As the guild leader of ShadowFang, he commanded authority not just through rank, but through reputation. ScarletDusk, a Lust Champion, stood at his side. They were both elite players, known across the server for their brutal presence in the recent Eternal Challenge.
It was that very event that had brought them here—to the treacherous expanse of the North Continent. Not for glory. Not even for conquest.
But for the hunt.

The High Elf Queen's quest had sparked a wildfire across the continents, and ShadowFang had answered the call like many of the top guilds. Hollow now stood near the edge of a settlement nestled close to the wilderness. It would be their last contact with civilization for a while. From this point forward, their journey would carry them far beyond the reach of cities—deep into the raw, untamed north.

"This is a pain," Hollow muttered, scanning the group as the last of his members gathered. "We've spent a fortune just to get here. But if the rewards are what they claim, then it's worth every damn coin."
He exhaled, then turned and started walking, leading the way forward. More than a hundred players followed behind—every one of them part of his guild.
ScarletDusk walked at his side.
They continued their march, the sound of armored boots and murmured conversation filling the air as the guild moved in formation.
"Finding this target," Hollow said, his voice laced with bitterness, "will do more than just earn us a reward. It'll deal a blow straight to Broken."
His scowl deepened as he spoke. "Because of him, we were humiliated in the Eternal Challenge. So now? We find his precious girl and make her ours."
ScarletDusk turned her head slightly, casting him a cool glance. "So, is it about the reward... or revenge?"

Hollow let out a dry laugh. "Why not both? If we pull this off, we get everything. Besides, who says we have to hand her over to the Queen right away? No—first we capture her, make a video, let the entire world see. Let Broken see. Let him regret ever crossing us."

A faint, knowing smile touched ScarletDusk's lips. "But first... since we're on the North Continent, I say we start by hunting a Giant. If we manage to kill even one, it'll give a serious boost to your Divine Champion blessing."

Hollow nodded. His blessing was unique—powerful. As an Envy Champion, he possessed the ability to summon perfect clones of anything he had previously killed. A Giant would make a terrifying addition to his arsenal.

"Yeah, we'll do both. Just make sure we don't fall behind. There are too many Divine Champions and high-tier guilds here already. Broken's made far too many enemies... and now he's going to feel the consequences." He chuckled darkly. "He made the mistake of standing out. Now everyone's watching."
ScarletDusk didn't reply, simply continued walking beside him as their guild swept down the edge of the town's stone streets like a shadowy tide.
The hunt had begun.

Some time later, the guild arrived at a designated staging area near the outskirts of the city, where several carriages waited to transport their members deeper into the wilds. A few of the transports were already loading, while others had yet to arrive.
Hollow and ScarletDusk lingered near the city gate, watching the final preparations—until a sudden disturbance drew their attention.
There was commotion at the main gate. Raised voices. Guards moving with urgency.

A figure stood before them, wrapped in a flowing black cape. His armor was pitch-black, polished and featureless, giving him a cold, ghost-like presence. But what stood out most—what immediately caught Hollow's eye—was the single, jagged horn protruding from the man's forehead.
A Demon. Unmistakably.
The argument between the guards and the figure carried clearly across the plaza.
"You need to show your face to enter."
"I'm fairly certain there's no such rule here," the stranger replied, calm but firm. "And I refuse."

"You think you make the rules?" one of the guards snapped. "There've been too many foreigners arriving in recent weeks. Our king issued this regulation. Show your full identity—or we'll kill you right here."
"I'll pay," the man said coldly. "Or I'll enter without your permission."
Hollow narrowed his eyes, intrigued, and turned to ScarletDusk. "Look at that player."
She followed his gaze, her expression sharpening. "He has Demon race traits."
"Yeah," Hollow muttered. "But I don't think he's with the Shadow Wolves. Doesn't match their look or their moves. He feels like a solo player. I've never seen anyone like him."
ScarletDusk considered that. "A solo Demon player who isn't local, and not with a guild? And he's bold enough to show up here, alone, in the middle of all this chaos?"
She smirked. "Maybe he's here for the same reason we are. To join the hunt. That takes guts."
Hollow nodded slowly. "Too many strong players are crawling out of the shadows lately. Makes you wonder how many others like him are already moving... and how many more we haven't seen yet."
They stood in silence for a few moments, both watching the tension build at the city gate. Then ScarletDusk spoke again, her tone casual but curious. "What are you thinking?"
"Well, you know... Frostedge is also a solo player," Hollow replied. "And he's damn powerful. But that guy's never shown the slightest interest in joining any guild."
"Yeah, he's too arrogant for that," she muttered. "And I hate it."
A wide grin spread across Hollow's face as the scene at the gate escalated. The guards were surrounding the mysterious horned player, clearly preparing to force him out or worse—cut him down.

Without hesitation, Hollow began striding forward, his footsteps firm. "A solo player like that," he said, almost to himself, "if I could get him to join my guild... now that would be interesting. Let's see if he's worth it."
He approached the gate just as the guards drew their weapons.
"Let him through," Hollow called out, his voice sharp and authoritative.
The guards turned, startled by the interruption—along with the horned player, who looked at Hollow with wary curiosity.
"He's with me," Hollow said firmly.
"Are you sure?" one of the guards asked, brows furrowing. "He doesn't look like—"
"I'm responsible for him," Hollow cut in. "In the name of ShadowFang."
There was a beat of silence.
Then, reluctantly, the guards lowered their weapons and stepped aside.
The mysterious player didn't say a word. He merely stepped forward, eyes briefly locking with Hollow's, and then walked past him as if nothing had happened.
Hollow fell into step beside him, a flicker of interest sparking in his eyes. As they made their way back toward the gathering crowd of ShadowFang members, Hollow glanced over with a grin.
This might get very interesting.
This player had deliberately concealed his gamertag, hiding it from view. But Hollow didn't mind. A lone traveler wasn't much of a threat—not to him, not to ShadowFang.
"So," Hollow began as they walked, keeping his tone casual, "you're not from the North Continent, are you?"
The mysterious player gave a small nod. "Yeah. I came from the East Continent."
"Huh... that's good to know," Hollow said with a grin. "And I assume I don't need to introduce myself, right?"
Again, the player nodded politely. "Of course not. Who doesn't know Hollow—the Envy Champion of ShadowFang? I appreciate you stepping in back there. Allow me to return the favor one day."

They continued walking side by side. ScarletDusk joined the conversation too, though the player still gave no indication of revealing his identity. No name, no class, no clear affiliations. Just a calm presence wrapped in mystery.
After a while, the player glanced around, then turned to Hollow. "I need to go. I want to set my respawn point here before heading out."
Hollow gave a small nod. "Sure. But before you go..." He paused, eyes narrowing with quiet curiosity. "You realize we might be after the same target, right?"
The horned player stopped, turning back to face him.
"And it'll be safer for you if you stick with us," Hollow continued. "I know this continent better than anyone you're likely to meet around here."
For a moment, the mysterious player said nothing. His expression was unreadable behind the black shadows of his armor and helmet. Then finally, he gave a slow nod.
"I'll be back in a few minutes," he said simply.
And with that, he turned and walked off into the city streets, disappearing into the crowd. Hollow watched him go, still smiling.
This wild hunt might prove even more entertaining than expected.
"Well, just remember—this player's identity is still completely unknown," ScarletDusk said.
"He'll reveal it eventually," Hollow replied. "Out there, during the journey. If not..."
He smirked,

"...we kill him. Simple as that. But until then, let's give him the benefit of the doubt. Another tool at our disposal isn't something to turn away. The more assets we control, the stronger our hand."
ScarletDusk gave a faint nod. "Yeah... I guess that makes sense."

I've never seen anyone like him."
ScarletDusk considered that.
"A solo Demon player who isn't local, and not with a guild?
And he's bold enough to show up here, alone, in the middle of all this chaos?"
She smirked.
"Maybe he's here for the same reason we are.
To join the hunt.
That takes guts."
Hollow nodded slowly.
"Too many strong players are crawling out of the shadows lately.
Makes you wonder how many others like him are already moving... and how many more we haven't seen yet."
They stood in silence for a few moments, both watching the tension build at the city gate.
Then ScarletDusk spoke again, her tone casual but curious.
"What are you thinking?"
"Well, you know...
Frostedge is also a solo player," Hollow replied.
"And he's damn powerful.
But that guy's never shown the slightest interest in joining any guild."
"Yeah, he's too arrogant for that," she muttered.
"And I hate it."
A wide grin spread across Hollow's face as the scene at the gate escalated.
The guards were surrounding the mysterious horned player, clearly preparing to force him out or worse—cut him down.
Without hesitation, Hollow began striding forward, his footsteps firm.
"A solo player like that," he said, almost to himself, "if I could get him to join my guild... now that would be interesting.
Let's see if he's worth it."
He approached the gate just as the guards drew their weapons.
"Let him through," Hollow called out, his voice sharp and authoritative.
The guards turned, startled by the interruption—along with the horned player, who looked at Hollow with wary curiosity.
"He's with me," Hollow said firmly.
"Are you sure?" one of the guards asked, brows furrowing.
"He doesn't look like—"
"I'm responsible for him," Hollow cut in.
"In the name of ShadowFang."
There was a beat of silence.
Then, reluctantly, the guards lowered their weapons and stepped aside.
The mysterious player didn't say a word.
He merely stepped forward, eyes briefly locking with Hollow's, and then walked past him as if nothing had happened.
Hollow fell into step beside him, a flicker of interest sparking in his eyes.
As they made their way back toward the gathering crowd of ShadowFang members, Hollow glanced over with a grin.
This might get very interesting.
This player had deliberately concealed his gamertag, hiding it from view.
But Hollow didn't mind.
A lone traveler wasn't much of a threat—not to him, not to ShadowFang.
"So," Hollow began as they walked, keeping his tone casual, "you're not from the North Continent, are you?"
The mysterious player gave a small nod.
"Yeah.
I came from the East Continent."
"Huh... that's good to know," Hollow said with a grin.
"And I assume I don't need to introduce myself, right?"
Again, the player nodded politely.
"Of course not.
Who doesn't know Hollow—the Envy Champion of ShadowFang?
I appreciate you stepping in back there.
Allow me to return the favor one day."
They continued walking side by side.
ScarletDusk joined the conversation too, though the player still gave no indication of revealing his identity.
No name, no class, no clear affiliations.
Just a calm presence wrapped in mystery.
After a while, the player glanced around, then turned to Hollow.
"I need to go.
I want to set my respawn point here before heading out."
Hollow gave a small nod.
"Sure.
But before you go..." He paused, eyes narrowing with quiet curiosity.
"You realize we might be after the same target, right?"
The horned player stopped, turning back to face him.
"And it'll be safer for you if you stick with us," Hollow continued.
"I know this continent better than anyone you're likely to meet around here."
For a moment, the mysterious player said nothing.
His expression was unreadable behind the black shadows of his armor and helmet.
Then finally, he gave a slow nod.
"I'll be back in a few minutes," he said simply.
And with that, he turned and walked off into the city streets, disappearing into the crowd.
Hollow watched him go, still smiling.
This wild hunt might prove even more entertaining than expected.
"Well, just remember—this player's identity is still completely unknown," ScarletDusk said.
"He'll reveal it eventually," Hollow replied.
"Out there, during the journey.
If not..."
He smirked,
"...we kill him.
Simple as that.
But until then, let's give him the benefit of the doubt.
Another tool at our disposal isn't something to turn away.
The more assets we control, the stronger our hand."
ScarletDusk gave a faint nod.
"Yeah...
I guess that makes sense."

chapters.title: Chapter 903 903 - Exactly what Broken Wanted
paragraphs: Broken had chosen to enter the city in his demon form. Though he still wore his full armor and kept his identity well concealed, the decision served a dual purpose: anonymity and deterrence. He hadn't come to cause trouble—just to find a respawn point, set it, and leave again before anyone took notice.
In truth, he could have snuck in and out without so much as a whisper. No one would've known.
But boredom got the better of him.

It was supposed to be a quick stop. Yet somehow, in a twist of irony, his path crossed with not just anyone—but two Divine Champions. And not just any Champions—these were members of one of the top guilds involved in the ongoing hunt for Ivana.
Broken recognized them instantly. He'd faced them during the last Eternal Challenge.
Hollow.

A strategist-type who specialized in cloning monsters he killed. Deadly enough on his own. But paired with his teammate—a support specialist who could temporarily lend her stats to Hollow's summoned clones—they were devastating. The synergy between them turned each summon into a fully armed war machine, capable of mimicking high-tier combat abilities.
And judging by the full guild force accompanying them, they weren't just scouting. They were here on a serious expedition.
Given the circumstances, Broken quickly realized that joining them might be the smartest option. At least for now.

If he played it right, he could gather valuable intel without drawing attention to himself. No need to tip his hand or reveal who he really was. Just another powerful stranger with useful skills, tagging along.

Besides, he'd already made sure his own team was secure. Beebot, the crawling golem, had been left in the care of his companions on the ship. With Grill, Bloom, and Ronan watching over it, they were more than capable of navigating the terrain on their own. They didn't need his guidance at the moment.
So, after setting the respawn point in the city, Broken circled back and rejoined Hollow's group.
He kept his posture relaxed, his tone neutral, careful not to show too much interest. Just helpful enough to be welcome—just detached enough to be unnoticed.
In the end, it was all about leverage.
And Broken intended to make the most of this opportunity.

He stood face-to-face with the guild leader, who stared down at him with a cold, appraising gaze. The man was taller—broad-shouldered and cloaked in thick armor—and he tilted his head just slightly, casting a faint shadow across his eyes.
"So," the man said, "what do you think? Want to tag along? I'm sure we could make something mutually beneficial out of traveling together."

Broken met his gaze without flinching, his voice flat and unreadable. "I might very well end up competing with your guild in this hunt. And yet, you're still willing to bring a stranger into your ranks?"
"This is the North Continent," Hollow said. "Not exactly a peaceful land. Out there, it's crawling with monsters. And most of them? They're level 300 or higher."
Broken said nothing.
"And you sure you came here alone?" Hollow asked, stepping just close enough for the challenge in his voice to feel heavier. "No allies hiding nearby?"

Broken gave a small, casual shrug. "I'm a solo player. Paid my way here and set my respawn point in the city, just in case I die doing something stupid against a monster way above my own. That's all."
A faint smile tugged at Hollow's lips, more like a smirk than anything. "I've got to respect that. Not many would brave this place alone. I assume you've got the power to back it up."

Broken's tone remained cool. "I like a good adventure. This seemed like the right kind of challenge. I didn't plan on joining any group—but then I ran into you. Might as well join the hunt while it's hot."
Hollow didn't hesitate.
"Good. So, what do you say?

"It'll be interesting," Broken said, his expression unreadable. "Besides, you're a guild with a solid reputation. It's an honor. And since you pulled me out of trouble... might as well see this through."
That earned him a sharper smile.
Hollow turned to his team and gave a quick signal. "Mount up!"

The members of the ShadowFang guild moved, each heading to their designated carriages. Most had closed tops, but Hollow himself led Broken toward the lead carriage: one with an open rooftop and elevated seats.
"Come," Hollow said, glancing over his shoulder. "There's plenty of room up here."
The driver, too, was a guild member.
Every person here was part of the same force.
And now, so was Broken.

Broken climbed up and took his seat beside ScarletDusk, their shoulders barely brushing as the carriage gently swayed beneath them. Across from them sat Hollow and the driver, who held the reins of the massive tamed beast pulling the lead vehicle.

Without delay, the convoy began to roll out, wheels crunching over snow-laced stone as they departed the city's edge. The gates closed behind them with a dull clang, sealing them off from the relative safety of civilization.
Beyond the walls stretched the wide, open expanse of the North Continent.

Dry trees stood tall across the barren landscape, their limbs gnarled and gray, dusted with patches of lingering snow. It was a world drained of color. The ground, cracked and lifeless in places, carried the feel of ancient decay. The air itself seemed still—too still.

This continent was infamous for its dead lands. The deeper you traveled, the stranger and more hostile the environment became. Towering forests of ancient, dying trees stretched endlessly across the horizon—most of them long dead, others frozen in a half-life, untouched by time or warmth.

Thick fog clung to the terrain, weaving between sharp hills and twisted roots, and the terrain itself was like nothing seen in other parts of Yunatea. The North Continent wasn't just a different land—it felt like a forgotten world entirely.
The journey was quiet. Hours passed with only the sound of the beast's breath and the crunch of wheels against frostbitten soil. Few words were exchanged.
But Broken could feel it.
Hollow was watching him. Carefully. Studying him not just as a potential ally—but as a mystery.
He hadn't yet found a way to dig deeper, hadn't pressed any questions. But the curiosity was there, simmering beneath the surface. The silence wasn't peace—it was calculation.
Broken found it amusing. Of course they were interested in him. A lone adventurer, strong enough to walk unafraid into a continent filled with monsters. That kind of figure always caught attention.
And to be fair, recruiting strong solo players had become a trend lately.
Forstedge came to mind—an infamous solo player whose reputation echoed across Yunatea. Truly solo. No party. No guild. No attachments.
Broken, on the other hand, wasn't really a solo player. He might not be surrounded by allies right now, but he was far from alone.
He had his spirits. His golems. A force entirely his own that he could summon in an instant.
That was the difference.
Without warning, the carriage lurched to a stop—then other carriage in the convoy halted in response.
Broken leaned forward, peering past the driver to the road ahead.
Monsters.

They were scattered across the terrain in clusters—humanoid in shape but dark and rough-skinned, as if their bodies had been sculpted from hardened clay. Their colors blended with the soil, but the flicker of their movement gave them away. There were dozens of them. And each one hovered around level 300.

The moment was tense but not chaotic. Members of the guild began climbing down from their carriages, weapons already drawn. A few positioned themselves on higher ground for ranged support, while others moved to flank the creatures directly.
Hollow and ScarletDusk, however, remained seated. The guild knew how to handle this.
Each monster was quickly engaged by a team of three to five players, forming coordinated battle clusters across the area.
Then Hollow turned toward Broken, his voice relaxed but tinged with challenge.
"So, Mr. Solo Player... interested in joining the action?"
Broken didn't answer.

He stood up slowly, dusted off his coat, and jumped down from the carriage with a soft thud. Without a word, he began walking toward the edge of the battlefield—directly toward the monsters that hadn't yet been targeted by any of the others.
Fortunately, he had equipped an item skin that masked the true appearance of his weapons, transforming even his most recognizable gear into something untraceable.
Now the question was—which weapon to use?
With a small grin, he summoned the Golden Bow of Artemis. Under the disguise, it appeared jet-black, streaked with writhing shadow energy that shimmered faintly across its curved surface.
He drew several arrows in a fluid motion and took aim.
[Explosive Arrow (Active Skill) Lv. 10 activated]
His eyes locked on a group of six monsters—rushing in tandem toward a group of guild members. Perfect.
He released the arrow.

A moment later, a deafening blast erupted in the distance. The ground trembled. Dust and snow kicked into the air. A wave of heat pulsed outward, and all heads turned toward the source of the explosion.
Even mid-fight, it was impossible to ignore.

Before the echo had fully faded, Broken nocked another arrow. And another. His movements were precise, cold, efficient. Each shot carved through the battlefield, clearing enemies with effortless power.
Just enough to make a statement.

Once the skirmish was under control, he lowered his bow and calmly walked back toward the lead carriage. As he climbed back into his seat, he caught Hollow watching him—expression shifted, no longer unreadable.
There was interest now.
Exactly what Broken wanted.

chapters.title: Chapter 904 904 - No Map for This
paragraphs: The group rode in silence, but after the display Broken had just delivered, the air felt heavier. As he stepped back into the carriage, all eyes followed him.
ScarletDusk leaned back, smirking. "Well, that was flashy."
Hollow chuckled, gaze fixed on Broken. "Explosive arrow with that kind of output? You're not just some drifter, are you?"
Broken shrugged, settling into his seat. "I like to keep a few surprises handy."
Hollow tilted his head slightly. "You've got the look. That presence. Let me guess... Divine Champion?"
ScarletDusk raised an eyebrow. "Definitely not Gluttony. Doesn't fit the profile. I mean we all know all those five."
"Right," Hollow nodded. "You don't match any of them."
Broken smiled faintly. "You seem very invested in Divine Champions."
"It's part of the job," Hollow replied smoothly. "Hard to run a top-tier guild without paying attention to high-value assets."
ScarletDusk leaned forward. "So? If not a Champion, then what? A Unique-grade class? Legendary maybe?"
Broken's tone stayed even. "You think too hard."
ScarletDusk leaned back again. "Well, whoever you are, that bow's not ordinary. You've got more going on than you let on."
"Maybe," Broken replied. "Maybe I just got lucky with the shot."
Hollow grinned. "If that's luck, I'd like some of it."
Broken had impressed them—enough to earn respect, but not trust. Just the way he liked it.
The truth behind the mask would only cause chaos if revealed. And Broken had no intention of letting anyone know he was here. Not in the North Continent.
To maintain the illusion, he occasionally appeared in Slumdon Town, letting himself be filmed by vloggers and swarmed by reporters desperate for updates. Honestly, it was a bit entertaining.
The benefit? His public presence in Slumdon sent a message. A quiet warning.

With news of his appearance spreading fast, Valantar City had backed off from launching another attack. They weren't ready to take chances—not after that devastating surprise strike they still couldn't trace. Not when Broken's involvement was a possibility.
The carriage rolled forward through snow and silence. Around him, Hollow and ScarletDusk exchanged light conversation, murmuring about tactics and recent guild skirmishes.
Broken didn't join in. He stared ahead, lost in his own thoughts.

They had been traveling for more than two weeks. Everyone stuck to a strict schedule—carefully managing login and logout times, staying sharp, and staying alive. Every monster encounter along the way kept them grounded. Nothing about this journey was easy. The higher they climbed, the harsher the path became, with terrain that constantly tested their endurance.
Then finally, they arrived.

The elevation they had reached now opened into something entirely different. It wasn't just a ridge or a clearing—it was massive. A colossal drop stretched out in front, so wide and vast it looked like the edge of another dimension.
And down below... was something else entirely.
From this height, it looked like an entirely separate world beneath them. A forest stretched across the basin of the chasm, snow covering most of its surface. It went on and on without end.
They wouldn't be able to take the carriages any further.
"Those trees..." ScarletDusk murmured, standing near Broken. "They're massive, right?"
Broken narrowed his eyes. "No, that's not normal. That's way beyond massive."
Even from this altitude, the trees below looked gigantic. Tower-sized trunks and canopies that seemed to scrape the top of the valley's mist.
Hollow stepped up beside Broken, his expression serious as he looked into the depths.
"According to the latest information," he said, "this is the area where the Dragon Princess was last sighted. Somewhere down there. But it's huge. We've got no detailed maps.
Broken crossed his arms, scanning the vast terrain below.
"And we can't bring the carriages down," Hollow added. "The path's too steep. Too narrow."
The decision was quick. They would leave the carriages here, at the ridge. It was pointless to force them any further.
The team got to work—unloading supplies, securing the area, and preparing for descent. If things went south, they'd need a safe way back.
Broken didn't move. He just stood there, silently staring into the mist-covered abyss.
Out of every place he had ever been in Yunatea, this one felt... different.
Hollow approached again. "We move tomorrow. I want everyone to be at full strength before we enter that place."
Yes. This wasn't just another forest.
This was something else entirely.
Five of ShadowFang's guild members suddenly stepped forward from the group, positioning themselves near the cliff's edge. One by one, without a word, they leapt into the open air.
For a moment, it looked like they were just falling—dropping into the massive expanse of mist and snow below.
Then, mid-air, each one activated their own unique flight skill.

Wings burst from one's back—crimson and feathered. Another twisted into a stream of wind, his body shimmering as he took the shape of a fast-moving gust. The others followed suit, each using different methods—gliding, shifting, even walking on air—until they became five distinct streaks descending into the abyss below.
Broken watched them disappear through the thick mist, vanishing toward the canopy.
"They're our scout crew," Hollow explained from beside him. "Elite squad. Each one has a different form of mobility. Short flight duration, but enough to land safely and secure the ground first."
He added, "Standard procedure for unknown terrain like this. We send them down first to scan the area, find stable spots to land, and check for hostiles."
Broken gave a short nod. "Makes sense."
"They'll mark safe zones for the rest of us," Hollow continued. "Don't worry, we'll move as soon as they send the signal."
"Looks like fun," Broken murmured.
Hollow smirked. "Depends on your definition."
"I'll wait for you down there," Broken said to the others without turning back.
Then he jumped.
Just like that.
No hesitation. No build-up. Just a clean, sudden dive off the cliff's edge into the vast fog-covered chasm below.
"What the?" Hollow blinked, taking a sharp step forward. "Did he just... jump?!"
ScarletDusk raised an eyebrow.
Hollow stared at the swirling mist where Broken had vanished. "Either he's stupidly reckless... or he knows exactly what he's doing."
There was a pause. Then Hollow exhaled through his nose, almost amused.
"...I'm betting on both."
Once Broken was out of sight from the rest, he whispered, "Pawpaw, invisibility.
A pulse of silent magic spread through the air as Pawpaw, activated the skill.
A second later, Polly—the flying fox—appeared in the open sky, wings wide and silent. Broken grabbed hold of her fur and swung himself onto her back.
They soared downward.
The air was colder here. Sharper. The wind cut through him like it had claws, but he ignored it. His focus was on what lay below.

They passed through the towering canopies—branches the size of full-grown trees, leaves as broad as rooftops. And finally, they landed on one of the highest limbs of a massive tree, its bark thick and ancient.
Broken stepped off and looked around.
"Damn... these trees are huge."
He ran a hand along the surface of the branch, feeling its solid, almost stone-like texture.
"The land of Giants?"
The sheer scale of this place was unnatural. Beyond anything he'd encountered before. Trees that rivaled mountains. Forests that swallowed the sky.
He crouched low, scanning the endless stretch of forest beneath him.
Broken raised his hand slightly, and moments later, Zepy, a sleek falcon-shaped golem, materialized beside him.
"Go," Broken said calmly. "Scout above the canopy. Stay high."
Zepy let out a low screech and launched into the air, cutting through the wind like a silent arrow.
But almost immediately, Broken's expression shifted.
The falcon golem flapped harder, trying to climb, but the higher it went, the more resistance it hit. The wind wasn't just strong—it was wild.

The golem tried to adjust, twisting through the gusts, but it couldn't gain altitude. Its wings flickered unnaturally. Then, with a sharp dip, Zepy was forced to retreat and loop back toward Broken, landing with a flutter beside him.
Broken narrowed his eyes, watching the sky with interest. "The wind's too aggressive up there, and Zepy's form is too small," he muttered.
"Yeah... you're not going to be much use here."

chapters.title: Chapter 905 905 - A Summon Too Far
paragraphs: The next morning, the forest remained just as still.

Broken was already waiting, perched on one of the upper branches, half-shrouded in fog and shadow. The sound of rustling leaves drew his attention, and soon, he spotted them—Hollow and his guild, emerging in a steady formation from between the twisted, towering trunks.
With a smooth motion, Broken leapt down, landing silently on the forest floor. He stood calmly, arms folded, as the large group approached, visibly worn from the long descent.
"How's the trip?" he asked.
"Hah. A complete waste of time," Hollow grumbled, brushing off his cloak. "But hey, adventure's adventure."
There was a moment of shared silence. It hit Broken then, somehow, without noticing it, they'd grown more familiar with each other. The edge of suspicion wasn't gone, but it was softer now.
Then Hollow nodded. "Come. You'll want to see this. It's something my scout team found earlier."

Without delay, they moved deeper into the forest. The trees here were older, stranger—roots twisted like sleeping serpents, and the canopy above blocked out so much light it felt like dusk, even in the morning. The temperature dropped with every step.
Eventually, they stopped.
In silence, they peered between two massive tree trunks.
What Broken saw took his breath for half a second.
A Giant.
A real, living, breathing giant.

It stood hunched, partially hidden between the trees, facing away. Its skin resembled cracked stone, weathered and old, layered with patches of moss. Its clothing was made from stitched leather and enormous slabs of metal—an armor-like outfit shaped for something five times the size of a normal human.
And... wait. The giant is sleeping? Sleeping—while standing?
This giant's long hair flowed all the way down his back, and his body remained eerily still, as if locked in a trance.
Broken checked the giant's stats.
Level 280. Pretty high. But not unmanageable—especially if he was alone.
"He is alone," Hollow said quietly.
And just like that, Broken knew exactly what this Envy Champion was thinking. He wanted to kill the giant... and summon him later as a clone?
Of course. That was exactly it.
Moments later, the entire team dispersed, moving in perfect sync to surround the area and cut off any chance of escape.
"You wait here," Hollow added with a thin smile.
Then it began.
Shots rang out—magic bolts, enchanted chains, projectiles from every direction. The giant's eyes snapped open in shock, his limbs suddenly bound by glowing chains that came from all angles.
"HUUUMAAAAANS!!"
"YOU DARE DISTURB MY SLUMBER?!"
"I WILL CRUSH YOUR PATHETIC WORLD!"
His roar thundered through the sky, shaking the very ground beneath their feet. But even with his fury unleashed, it was already too late.
Arrows, spells, explosions—dozens of attacks rained down before he could even break free.
The giant staggered.
Then—THUD!!
His knee slammed into the ground with a tremor that echoed across the cliffs.
Seconds later, he collapsed fully—defeated.
ShadowFang Guild had done it.
But as the dust settled and their victory became clear... Broken couldn't shake the feeling in his gut.
If the other giants found out one of their own had been killed like this...
They wouldn't forgive it.
And this would only be the beginning.
And just like that, things calmed down again.
The tension faded, replaced by cheers and grins. The entire guild stood tall, proud of what they had accomplished. And Hollow—well, he finally got exactly what he wanted out of this journey.
"Hahaha! See? That was way too easy," he said with a smug laugh, basking in the applause around him.
"Now then... let's see just how amazing this new giant of mine really is."
He stepped back.
His guildmates cleared a space in front of him, forming a loose circle. Glowing lines appeared on the ground—a summoning formation.
With a brief pulse of light, the clone of the giant emerged. Massive, silent, and imposing, the newly summoned figure stood motionless like a statue, awaiting orders.
The crowd of guild members erupted into cheers, applause, and over-the-top praise.
"That's our genius Hollow! Even gods would be jealous!"
"You didn't just beat the giant—you collected him like a trophy!"
"I swear Hollow could tame a dragon if he felt like it."
Well... Broken smirked. The way the guild members were showering Hollow with praise felt less like admiration—and more like flattery taken to absurd levels.
Too much bootlicking, he thought. And Hollow? He was absolutely loving it.
Then, Hollow turned to him with a wide grin.
"So, I'm not surprised you're strong, my friend. But surely, we Divine Champions... we're on a whole different level. You saw it yourself—just how incredible my new summon is."
Broken paused.
Then, with a straight face and dramatic tone, he echoed the guild's earlier praise, mimicking their style perfectly.

"Truly astonishing, Hollow. If I weren't standing here, I'd swear you rewrote the rules of the world just now. I mean... who else could bend a giant to their will while smiling? You're not just a Champion. You're practically a divine script error."
The guild members burst into laughter, and a few even clapped.
Hollow, of course, took it at face value.
"Haha! See? Even you admit it!" he beamed, unsummoning the giant with a simple gesture.
Then Hollow walked over and gave Broken a firm pat on the shoulder.
"Keep working at it. Who knows—maybe one day the Sin Gods will smile upon you too and toss you a shiny toy like this. Hahaha!"
Just how many summons does this guy actually have?
The journey continued.
Their footsteps echoed across the forest floor. Until it suddenly stopped.
Because in front of them now stood something far larger than they had expected.
A serpent.
Not just large. Monstrous.

Its body coiled around ruined towers like a god of old, each scale the size of a shield, its fangs longer than a full-grown man. The moment it sensed them, its head snapped forward with a bone-rattling hiss that shook the earth.
Broken narrowed his eyes. "You've got to be kidding."
Without hesitation, Hollow raised his hand. "Let's make this interesting."
A magic circle ignited beneath his feet.
With a crack of light, the giant from before emerged once more. The giant let out a thunderous roar and charged at the serpent.
And then, chaos.
The serpent struck, but Hollow didn't even flinch. With smooth gestures, he directed his summon like a war conductor.
And then, without warning, he unsummoned the giant mid-combat.
The others froze. Even Broken raised an eyebrow.
But Hollow? He stepped forward himself.
In a blur of black mist and energy, he single-handedly took down the serpent.
Dodging venom strikes. Deflecting attacks. Landing devastating blows. Until finally—he stood on the serpent's unmoving head, brushing dust off his shoulder.
He turned back to the others, grinning.
"See? I don't even need the summon. But I can have as many as I want from this place. Pretty cool, right?"
The guild roared in approval. More flattery. More awe.
But Broken... He just stared, arms crossed, silent.
"Multiple summons like this... and he doesn't even need them? Is he collecting an army?"
Because if this kept up, Hollow wouldn't just be a Champion.
He'd be a one-man raid boss.
And this reminds me that so far Broken had only been watching while this guy collects an army from this wild area.
During the journey, Broken kept in touch with the rest of his guild.
Through private messages, he received an update from SexyGrill. Her team was currently exploring a different region of the continent, separate from where Broken and the others were.
That was good.
It meant they were covering more ground—doubling their chances of finding clues, especially the one that mattered most right now.
Ivana. If she was truly somewhere in this place... then why? What was she doing in a land like this?
Broken couldn't shake that question from his mind.

The forest path twisted on, slowing their pace. Massive roots cut through the earth like jagged scars, and the canopy above blocked nearly all sunlight. Occasionally, the party stopped to log out and rest, carefully syncing their schedules to log back in at the same time.
Not easy—especially when they came from different countries and time zones.
But even so, they pressed forward, maintaining cohesion.
And along the way... they fought.
Several monsters attacked them during the trek, and none of them were normal.
Everything here was massive.
Serpents with heads the size of wagons. Wild boars taller than trees. Even the insects they spotted along the way seemed to move like armored machines.
It wasn't that the players had shrunk...
It was the world around them that had grown.
Each encounter tested their reflexes, coordination, and stamina. Most of the monsters were over level 250, which meant even a moment of carelessness could cost them their lives.
Yet, what disturbed Broken more than the combat... was the atmosphere.
The deeper they went, the more he felt it.
A pressure. A presence.
Something was watching them from within the trees.
And in that moment...
A single notification blinked across his vision.

chapters.title: Chapter 906 906 - The Giants Among Us
paragraphs: Leon stepped out of his capsule device and made his way to the center of the room, where he spotted Freya lounging casually.
"Come on, Leon, let's watch the mess you've made," she said cheerfully, not even bothering to look his way.

He sat down beside her, eyes drawn to the screen before them. It showed a fierce battle unfolding between the ShadowFang guild and five towering giants. Monsters that had emerged just moments before Leon, in-game, made his escape, leaving the others to fend for themselves.

The giants were enormous, their sheer size overwhelming, and each wielded colossal swords capable of slicing through multiple opponents in a single swing. Even with over a hundred guild members on the field, their numbers were dwindling fast.
"You know, this is the first time giants like these have shown up in such numbers, and it's all being broadcast live," Freya commented casually, munching on something from a bag of chips.
Leon reached over, grabbed a few himself, and chuckled.
"They really thought they could take these giants down."
The players had gone out of their way to stream the battle, hoping to attract sponsors and rack up views. Losing face was the last thing they wanted.
"What do you think they'll say once they find out you ran away like a coward the moment those giants appeared?"

"They don't even know who I am. And I'm sure they've already started getting suspicious since I haven't shown my face. But who cares, really. At first, I planned to rob them and wipe them out myself. But luckily, they turned out to be the perfect bait to lure out these giants."
"You've definitely entered your villain arc, huh?"
Leon let out a sigh and smiled. "That's exactly why I'm using the demon identity, isn't it?"
The battle didn't last long. Once the footage cut off, it was clear—even with that many players, they hadn't managed to defeat the five giants.
"And that's it. We've just witnessed the raw power of the giant race firsthand," Freya said as she switched to another channel.
"And we haven't even seen the Sin wielder yet, huh?"

"Good luck then," Freya said, her voice calm but watchful.

chapters.title: Chapter 907 907 - Unique Is Not Enough
paragraphs: Broken stepped once again onto the floating island of Vensalor, and right away, he could see just how much had changed. The island, once a natural haven of rolling hills, trees, and lakes, now buzzed with life and structure.

Though the buildings had been crafted to blend harmoniously with the environment, the paved roads and the towering castle—rising near the highest peak—made it clear that transformation was well underway.
"Good evening, King Broken!" Livelywood came running toward him, grinning and waving excitedly.
"Hey. The progress looks great. How far along are we?"
"Around seventy percent, but it won't be long before we're able to house even more people here. Maylock also mentioned he's starting to train the knights to get used to the island's layout."
Broken frowned slightly. "He's not planning to stir up a war anytime soon, is he?"

"Ah, haha, maybe he's just a little bored. Things have been quiet in the Vensalor Kingdom lately. After that failed assault from Valantar City, the other kingdoms have been hesitant to make any moves."
Broken scratched the back of his head. "Well, I've got a few things to take care of. Have a nice day, Livelywood."

With that, he summoned Polly and climbed onto the fox's back. Taking off into the sky, he soared above the island, marveling at the view. Who knew how much money had already been poured into building this floating paradise?

What mattered now was that the main castle, already completed. Built primarily in white stone, it was partially veiled by flowering vines and lush trees along its edges. He landed on the balcony of the structure, which was now his stronghold. Inside, he had a private blacksmithing workshop. Finally, a place where he could work on his craft in peace.

Broken stepped into his private chamber, a wide, open space dedicated to his blacksmithing craft. At the center stood a large forge and a sturdy anvil, perfectly placed for his work. A wide window opened out toward the sea, offering a breathtaking view. But he always kept it closed during forging, to maintain the fire's stability.

He took out two blueprints and spread them across the table. One was for a bow, the other for a sword. A smile tugged at his lips. These blueprints had been given to him by Alora, meant as gifts for their children. Elaris and Caelum.
They were growing fast. No surprise, really. One was half-elf, half-human, and the other, a Fae.

Elaris had taken a strong liking to swords. It wasn't surprising; she'd clearly inherited that from Alora, who herself was a masterful swordswoman. Broken could already see so much of her mother in her. Sharp, spirited, and fiercely determined. Elaris never tolerated laziness and made sure everyone pulled their weight.
Caelum, on the other hand, was calmer, more mature—even though Elaris had been born first. His quiet confidence set him apart, and to Broken's delight, the boy had developed a fondness for the bow.
And now, these two blueprints—Broken had cleared his schedule, setting aside the next few days, maybe even a week, just to focus on crafting these weapons.

Both designs held extraordinary potential, their quality ranging from Unique to Legendary. Despite being scaled down in size to suit children, the power within them was anything but small. These weren't just toys, they were masterpieces in the making.
More than anything... Broken lowered himself onto his chair and began setting up his tools. It had been months. Maybe even over a year, since he last managed to craft a legendary-grade item.

It felt deliberate, almost like the system had nerfed him on purpose. The thought alone made his blood boil. He needed just one more legendary-grade item. Just one. That should've secured his position as the first player in the game to attain a Legendary Class.
Everything was in place now. His workstation gleamed under the warm forge light, tools aligned, materials laid out with precision. Taking a deep breath, he shifted his focus entirely.
He lit the forge, the flames flickering to life with a familiar roar, and the room instantly filled with the heat and hum of purpose.
It was time to begin.

A day passed, then another. During that time, Broken remained in constant coordination with SexyGrill, who was still stationed on the North Continent, monitoring the areas where the giants were most likely to be found.
Broken could join her at any moment. His golem ship was already positioned near the region in question. All he had to do was warp over.
He'd also caught wind of the growing number of guilds flooding into the North Continent—especially after the recent footage of the giants began circulating. He sighed at the thought.
These players... they were always so hungry to kill anything they believed might offer a grand reward.
They didn't realize the true danger. There might be entire legions of giants hidden within those frozen lands. Even the Ancestral Sin Champions themselves had chosen not to confront them directly.

For centuries, the giants had isolated themselves within the North Continent. Only now, in this modern age, were outsiders beginning to inch closer to the long-forbidden territory that was their home.

On the seventh day, Broken was finally ready to begin the final phase of crafting the two weapons for his children. Everything was prepared, the materials refined, the forge at perfect heat. He stood before the anvil, focused and steady—until a knock echoed through the room, followed by the slow creak of the door opening.
A woman stepped inside, dressed in a deep red noble gown. Her crimson hair was tied neatly behind her, radiating elegance even in the warmth of the forge.
"Alora," he murmured softly.
For the past three days, he had invited her to stay on the island—partly because she wanted to witness the final forging process herself.
Broken paused his work, looking her way.
"You're not going to let your work get interrupted just because I walked in, are you? Should I leave then?" she asked, smiling gently.
"No..." he replied in a low voice. "More like..."
He set down his hammer and stood upright.
"Look at you, covered in smoke. Don't tell me—" she started, her smile widening, a soft giggle escaping her lips.
"I need fuel to finish this job," he said as he stepped closer.
Then, without another word, he pulled her into an embrace, holding her tightly.
She laughed quietly, resting her hands against him. "Won't this throw off your focus? I thought no one could disturb you when you're working."
"You're part of me. So this is okay."
And with that, Broken wrapped his arms around her even tighter, grounding himself in that moment of warmth before returning to the fire.

They stayed like that for a while, just holding each other. Long enough for the storm of thoughts inside Broken's head to settle. After some time, he gently released her and turned back to his workstation, the fire still glowing warmly.
Alora took a seat nearby, close enough to watch him work, her presence calm and reassuring.
"I hope they'll like these weapons," he said softly as he adjusted one of the forging tools.
"They're going to love them. If I hadn't stopped them, they'd already be begging to join you on your sea trip.
Broken gave a faint smile. "They'll have to wait two more years for that."
"Five years," Alora countered immediately.
Broken glanced her way. "Three more years."
"Five."
"Four? That's too long."
"You know they're still kids."
He chuckled under his breath. "Maybe I'll get back to working on the tower. If I'm lucky, I'll find two more keys, so they can reach this place more easily."
Because the truth was, the only other way to reach this floating island was by sea—a voyage that took weeks and was far from safe.
Sure, he could request an escort from Queen Nerisa's forces, but that could wait. For now, he had weapons to finish, and dreams to forge for the future.
Broken moved into the final phase. He started with the bow.

The weapon had a sleek, green-hued design with an elegant curve. Set into one side was a gleaming crystal—formed from the core of an Epic-grade monster. He handled it with the utmost care, entering a precise rhythm as he polished and sealed the last segments of the weapon.
Then, suddenly, a soft green aura radiated from the bow.
"Unique grade?" Alora said, watching the glow dance through the air.
"Yes, Unique grade," Broken replied, his tone steady.
Alora smiled and nodded. "That's more than enough."
But Broken shook his head slowly. "Unique is the minimum grade this blueprint can yield. Anyone skilled enough to craft it would end up with a Unique-grade weapon."
Alora raised an eyebrow. "You do realize there aren't many Master-rank blacksmiths in the world, right? The only one I know besides you is Mr. Fokil."
Broken gave a small nod, then turned his attention to the sword.

It was a slender blade with a deep black hilt, a gleaming silver edge, and a crimson crystal embedded near the guard. He began the finishing process—each movement deliberate, every strike echoing purpose. His hand trembled slightly as he worked, the pressure of this moment heavier than before.
As he completed the last touch, the aura that erupted from the sword was not green, nor blue. But something far more rare.
"Broken?" Alora whispered, breath catching.
Broken stood frozen for a moment, staring at the glow.
"Legendary-grade," he said at last, his voice low, stunned.
A smile broke across his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 908 908 - Master of the Eternal Forge
paragraphs: [You have successfully completed the quest: Path of the Legendary Blacksmith]
[Your tireless hammering, relentless crafting, and frankly ridiculous level of patience have finally paid off.]
[As a reward for completing this quest, you will receive +25 stat points.]
[Additionally, you've been granted the Legendary Class: Master of the Eternal Forge.]
[SKILL EVOLUTION DETECTED...]
Broken stood still as the system message finally appeared before him. Just... how long had that quest been sitting in his log? And only now, after all this time, he'd managed to complete it.
And this meant, yes. He should be the first player to unlock a Legendary Class.
He only skimmed through the skill upgrade notification, not even fully reading the details. The weight of what he'd just achieved was already overwhelming.
Turning to Alora, he flashed a wide grin—one that said everything without a single word. He'd done it.
"So, you finally got it?" she said.
"Yes! I'm officially a Legendary Blacksmith now! Yes!"
Unable to contain his joy, Broken stepped forward and pulled Alora into another tight embrace, holding her close like the victory itself.
Alora let out a soft laugh as Broken hugged her tightly. She returned the embrace, then spoke in a gentle, affectionate tone, filled with pride.
"You finally made it to the top... I always knew this day would come. And there's no one more deserving of that title than you. I'm proud of you, my husband."
Broken and Alora had returned to the castle, and without delay, he presented the two newly crafted weapons to the eager little ones waiting before them.
Elaris and Caelum's eyes lit up with pure excitement as they reached out to claim their respective weapons. Elaris took the sword, and Caelum the bow.
Elaris squealed, her voice high with joy, "Waaah! This is so cool! I'm gonna slice up all the monsters with this! I'll be the best monster hunter ever!"
Caelum, more reserved, held the bow carefully and looked up at Broken with a gentle smile. "Thank you, Papa. It's beautiful. I'll take good care of it."

Of course, it was unusual for children their age to even hold real weapons. But these two weren't ordinary kids. They were easily ten times stronger than normal children. Both had already begun sword lessons, and Caelum had even shown skill in archery.

Alora stepped closer to them, her tone warm yet firm. "These weapons will be yours when the time is right. You'll be allowed to use them after you've properly studied under Imperial Knight Lionell. Understood?"
Elaris puffed her cheeks and pouted. "But I wanna use it now! I can hunt a monster today, I promise!"
Caelum nodded politely. "I understand, Mama. I'll keep learning."
Elaris turned to her brother with a dramatic sigh. "You're just scared. All you can use is a wooden bow anyway!"
Caelum raised an eyebrow and replied with a calm tone, "You still fall over half the time and swing in the wrong direction when you use a sword, Elaris."
Elaris spun toward him, fuming. "That's because I'm still growing! Soon I'll be as strong as Knight Lionell, just watch!
Then, after a beat, she puffed out her chest and grinned. "I am cool, right? I know I can do it! I'll show everyone! Let's gooo!"
"Papa, take me to hunt demons, please?" she added, eyes shining with excitement.
Broken couldn't help but laugh, the warmth of the moment washing over him. He scooped up both kids into his arms, chuckling as Alora took the weapons from their small hands with a knowing smile.

Each day brought new progress, both of them growing steadily under the direct guidance of a royal Imperial Knight.

"King, you've returned," she said with enthusiasm.
"Any updates, Mizuki?"
"Yes... Come, look at this."

"I believe I've found the area where the giants may be living. It's an open space, which could be dangerous to approach alone. "Yes."
Mizuki swiped her hand, and a map floated into view in front of them—detailed, with terrain markers and flight paths carefully marked.
"You'll want to follow this route. Flying will get you there faster. I've already highlighted the danger zones you should avoid. Stick to the course, and you'll approach the target undetected."
"Thanks, Mizuki. Good work."
"Alright, King... good luck out there."
Broken stepped out onto the ship's dock, the wind cold and sharp against his face. Without hesitation, he summoned Polly, the sleek fox mount materializing in a shimmer of light.

With a flash of dark mist, the small cat demon appeared nearby, stretching lazily before flicking its tail and trotting over.

Broken gave the cat a gentle stroke between the ears. "You can head back once we reach our destination."

chapters.title: Chapter 909: The Giants’ Watch
paragraphs: It had been quite a long journey... moving through the forest with those towering trees made Broken feel like nothing more than a tiny insect when Polly soared past them.
Fortunately, Polly's mana regeneration was higher than the mana required to keep her flying, so even with such a long flight, it was still possible for her to continue.

The only real challenge was Pawpaw, who occasionally had to turn off his invisibility skill. Because of that, they often had to land on the large branches to rest and recover their stamina for a while.

They could easily return to Vensalor Island, wait for Pawpaw to regain his stamina, and let Polly recover as well. After that, they would be ready to head back toward the North Continent and continue their journey.
It was going to take at least three or four days, a long trip indeed, but still much faster than crossing the region on foot.
The place was freezing, strangely so, as if the cold in this game world was sharper than the autumn chill outside in real life.
The path Broken followed, carefully provided by Mizuki, gave them a safe route through the forest, with only a small chance of running into monsters along the way.
Even so, Broken made no attempt to hunt any monsters along the way. His only focus was to reach his destination as quickly as possible.

At one point, they stopped behind a line of massive trees, stepping out of the forest where they caught sight of a structure rising in the distance among the trunks. And damn, it turned out to be the dwelling of giants.

The houses looked strange, though at first glance their shape seemed ordinary. Built from enormous stones with equally massive doors, they stood tall and silent. Yet, not a single giant was seen nearby.
From what he knew, giants rarely stayed inside their homes. Most of the time, they would be out hunting or busy with other tasks.
At the very least, information about the giants had started to spread more widely now, especially since more players had begun exploring this region to learn about them.
They decided to skip venturing deeper into the giants' territory and instead circled around through the forest, as Broken had another place he wanted to visit afterward.
Eventually... They emerged into a wide open field, where a raging blizzard was tearing across the land.
"We need to head down, Polly.
Polly swooped toward the ground, landing in an area swallowed by darkness as the storm howled and snow whipped through the air.
"We can't fly in weather this bad," Broken said as he climbed down from the white fox.
The moment his feet touched the ground, Polly vanished, leaving only Broken with Pawpaw, who was curled up and napping comfortably on his shoulder.
"I'm tired. I wanna go home," the little cat complained, sounding grumpy.
"You know we're here to find Ivana, right?" Broken replied with a smile.
"You've told me that over and over, Broken. But we still haven't found her."
"I just hope the information we've got this time is accurate. We'll need to keep pushing on for a while longer."
With that, Broken summoned his crawling carriage golem. It appeared instantly, its frame quickly coated in falling snow.
He leapt up and settled on top of it, where he could keep a better watch on the surroundings. Using his flying golem for scouting was out of the question in such terrible weather.
"Why does Ivana have to hide in a place like this? Couldn't she have chosen somewhere better?"
Broken didn't answer. Even he wasn't sure they would find her here. But this was the deepest part of the giants' territory, a place where ordinary players would struggle to reach.
If they traveled on the ground, they would constantly run into monsters and even the roaming giants who patrolled the area.
And if they tried flying... Well, not many players had both the means of aerial transport and the ability to conceal themselves at the same time.
Broken, however, had both. With Polly to carry him through the skies and Pawpaw's invisibility skill to keep them hidden, he could do what others could not.
The carriage was forced to stop as night fell, the blizzard raging harder than ever. Luckily, it remained cloaked in invisibility.
A heavy thudding sound echoed closer and closer. Broken kept his eyes fixed ahead until finally, shapes emerged from the storm. Two giants, each nearly five times his height, clad in heavy armor.
"I sensed movement around here, but I don't see anything," said the first giant, a tall figure with long black hair.
"You're imagining things. No one would dare come this close," the other giant, bald and broad-shouldered, replied.
Watching how strictly they guarded this place, Broken felt certain now. Something important was being protected here.
"Even in a blizzard like this," one of them muttered.
"I'll keep checking the area. I'm sure the alarm wasn't wrong," the first added.
Fortunately, Broken remained hidden within invisibility, safe for the moment. Still, this was a clear sign that he needed to move with even greater caution.
After a while, the two giants finally moved on, their heavy footsteps echoing even through the darkness and the howling storm, until they faded into the distance behind.
"So they really do have an alarm? Maybe that's why Mizuki warned me not to fly around here. Though honestly, even without one, flying in this weather would already be nearly impossible."
The carriage pressed forward again, still cloaked in invisibility, though the snow kept piling heavily over it as they pushed through the blizzard.
Then... Broken spotted a lone figure ahead, its silhouette faint against the storm's curtain of snow.
He quickly signaled Beebot to stop, hoping the figure would simply pass by and vanish into the white.
But instead, it stepped forward. Closer. Straight toward them. Without a doubt, its path was leading directly to Broken.

chapters.title: Chapter 910: Ravengar of Wrath
paragraphs: Broken froze in place as the approaching figure continued walking toward them. This one was even taller than the previous two. Could it be someone of higher rank? Maybe someone far more important than the others.
When the giant finally stepped into view, its form became clear. A massive being with dark bluish skin, clad in heavy armor, and two sharp horns rising from its head.
Wait, horns? Weren't those supposed to be traits of demons? Some subspecies of giants might have them too, but this one radiated a very different kind of aura.
Broken tried inspecting the giant's status. Only the name appeared, Ravengar. While every stat was replaced by question marks. This was a first for him.
If not a single stat could be read, then either the giant's level was far too high... or it knew how to hide its true identity.
Broken stayed perfectly still, watching as the giant stopped a short distance away. It didn't move, didn't speak. Silent and still, as if waiting for something.
Then... after a long pause, the giant slowly turned its head. Looking straight at Broken.
Wait... could it actually see him?
The giant remained motionless, staring in his direction without a word or any other sign of intent.
Then, suddenly, it turned away. One step, two steps, its heavy footsteps thundering through the snow as it walked off into the storm.
"Should we follow him?"
Gaia appeared beside Broken, sitting casually with her legs crossed. "That giant is suspicious. He's hiding his true identity."
"Exactly what I thought," Broken replied quietly.
Broken still kept his gaze fixed ahead. "I've had a bad experience with someone whose status was just as suspicious as this."
"He did tell you to follow him," Gaia continued.
Broken gave a faint smile. "It's actually pretty obvious, even though he tried to hide it. He kept looking in my direction for quite a while."
"That could be a trap too."
"There's one thing we need to remember," Broken went on. "If we need to make contact with them as soon as possible, and if he's already aware of my presence, then he must have something to say.
He nodded slightly. "Let's take a chance on this."
Broken nodded again and signaled the crawling carriage to move forward.
The giant's strides were long, and even pausing for a moment left Broken far behind. Fortunately, after pushing forward through the raging blizzard, the giant's figure came into view once more.
If such a blizzard happened in the real world, any ordinary human would have frozen to death within minutes.

The journey went on, and Broken kept his distance, making sure they didn't fall too far behind. It took quite a long time. More than an hour, and the farther they went, the wilder the landscape became.

Even though it was an open field wide enough to seem ordinary for a creature that size, to someone like Broken, it was full of hazards. There were deep cracks splitting the ground, almost invisible through the worsening blizzard, and they had to cross them carefully.
Then... far ahead, a faint light appeared. It shone clearly even through the thick snowstorm surrounding them.
The raging blizzard suddenly stopped when Beebot darted ahead and came to a halt.
Broken turned around. No, the blizzard hadn't stopped. They had entered an area where the snow simply didn't fall at all.
He looked forward again and saw a formation of towering rocks, jagged and sharp from his perspective. The giant stood right in the middle of four of those massive stone spires.
Between the four jagged formations glowed a faintly shining magic circle. Its light dim but steady, pulsing through the air like it was alive.
A deep growl rumbled from the front. Broken focused his gaze just as the giant turned around and looked straight at him.
"How dare someone trespass into this sacred ground!" the giant's voice thundered.
At that very moment, something surged from behind Broken. A domain unfolded in an instant, closing off the entire area.
He spun around to check it. His eyes widened. It was a level 450 domain!
Damn! They were trapped?!
Broken quickly stood up and released his stealth mode, his gaze fixed on the giant standing not too far away.
"I mean no harm. There's just something I need to check in this place," he said calmly.

"Do you think you can just walk into someone's territory and casually say you have something to check?" the giant's voice rumbled. "Have humans forgotten how to behave properly? You've only grown worse as time goes on."
Broken shook his head. "I might look human, but we're players."
"I know exactly who you are," the man interrupted. "And I also know that you're the Sloth Champion."

Broken frowned slightly. "I can guess as much, considering you noticed my presence the moment I arrived. And..." he paused for a moment, thinking, "am I also right to assume that you're... the Wrath Champion?"
The giant's expression remained cold and stern as he stepped forward, each stride sending a deep thud through the ground.
