chapters.title: Chapter 911 - No Way Forward
paragraphs: Leon stepped out of the capsule device with a long sigh. He was genuinely overwhelmed this time. Maybe this was the first time in a long while that he truly felt like he had run out of answers, like there was no clear way forward anymore.

He simply walked into the central lounge and dropped onto one of the sofas, not bothering to think about anything else. After that, he sent Freya a 9message explaining everything that had happened, hoping she could at least give him some advice, or maybe just a few comforting words.

Then, later that evening, Freya decided to stop by. The two of them planned to hang out at the café downstairs, where Leon had already reserved the private seating area separated from the main café. It was a balcony overlooking the street, enclosed by a glass door that kept it away from the noise and the crowd.
It was not because he was arrogant or anything. He had honestly never expected people to come here on purpose just to see him. Like, seriously?

At first, Leon had opened this café simply as a place where he could relax and spend his own time. That was why he had designed it with such a spacious layout. It was never meant to accommodate a large number of customers. But now... every single seat was actually occupied.

Maybe he really should open the upper floor as a dining area. It would probably bring in extra income as well, enough to help cover the operating costs of this building, which turned out to be far more expensive than he had expected.

The brown-haired girl arrived wearing a long coat and a pair of glasses. With her usual confident stride, she pushed open the balcony door, set her bag beside her chair, then sat down and casually crossed her legs.
"I didn’t know you’d put this much effort into preparing a private spot for our date, huh?"
"Well, I was actually hoping it’d be a lot quieter than this, but apparently it’s this crowded."

"Congratulations, Leon. You’re famous now. More and more people are logging into Immortal Legacy, you know. Especially around here. Even the game centers have gotten a lot busier. You could even open one on the unused floor upstairs. I’m sure it’d attract plenty of people."
"You never stop thinking about business, huh, Freya?"
She laughed softly.

"I’m just waiting for your approval, and I’ll take care of everything. Besides, you don’t need this many floors just for yourself, do you? Your daily routine is incredibly boring. You just play games, train, and hang out in this café. You barely even go outside, and every time you ask me to meet you, it’s always here."
"I thought this place matched your taste. You were the one who helped design it, remember?"
"Yes, but there are so many amazing places out there. Overseas too. I’m pretty sure you can afford to travel now, can’t you?"
Leon let out another sigh before giving a small nod.
"I think so... especially after what happened to Broken inside the game."
After that, the discussion shifted back to what was actually happening inside the game.
"I won’t be able to leave that domain. It’s far beyond the level I can handle. And I can’t teleport out using any method either."
Freya nodded.

"You could just wait until your level goes up, couldn’t you? If you stay there long enough, you’ll keep gaining experience eventually. Once your level is high enough to meet the requirement to break through the domain, you should be able to leave."
"Yes, but that’ll take a very long time."
"Oh, right. I completely forgot. What level are you now?"
"203? Wow. It’s been a while since I last checked, so I had no idea you’d gotten that high already."
"Yeah. Ever since I started spending so much time traveling across the sea, time has been passing really fast. And somehow... It’s already October."
Freya gave a slow nod.
"Then I don’t think it’s realistic for you to reach level 350 anytime soon just so you can leave that domain."
Leon nodded again. "We could bring everyone from Vensalor and launch an attack against the giants."
Freya shook her head.
"If the giant you met really is the Champion of Wrath, then I’m sure he’s already seen that possibility. His ability lets him see the branching futures created by every action he takes."
"So that means he already knows what could happen in the future. That’s why he trapped me and locked me inside that place."
"It’s more than that," Freya continued. "We need to force him to reveal what he’s actually hiding."
"So... we just launch the raid.

"I’m sure he’s already taken that into account as well. Starting a war between the players and the giants might be exactly what he’s trying to provoke." Freya paused to think for a moment. "Doesn’t that seem possible? He knows players have the advantage of respawning after they die. The giants, on the other hand, would be the ones paying the real price."
Leon picked up his cup of coffee and took another sip.
"I guess not every problem can be solved with brute force."
"That’s just the way you think. Hey, you, Broken," Freya said more firmly. "Not everything can be solved with brute force."
"It worked before. I got this far through pure brute force."
Freya could only let out a quiet sigh. Leon then set his cup back down on the table.
"Tell me, Freya. Where do you think would be a fun place to go on vacation?"
"What? Where did that come from?"
"A vacation. Yes, a vacation. You’re the one who suggested it earlier."
"Are you asking me to go on a trip with you?"
"You’re the one who brought it up first."
"You think I’m that easy to invite on a vacation, Leon? I’m not..."
"Fine, we’ll invite everyone else too. So where? Tell me."
"Well... I wouldn’t actually mind if it were just the two of us."
Leon laughed instead.
"Just tell me. And don’t say Korea again."
"Then right next to Korea. Japan. What do you think?"
"Well... we’ll leave tomorrow."

chapters.title: Chapter 912 - Vacation... Right?
paragraphs: Leon sat in the passenger seat, carefully sipping the coffee from his tumbler. It was still hot, so he had to be careful. After another sip, he let out a quiet breath and smiled faintly as the morning sunlight streamed through the window while the car sped along the road.
"I thought you’d bring your wife and kid too, King," he said, glancing at the man driving beside him. The large-built man almost looked too big for the driver’s seat.
King simply sighed at the question.

"You know my kid’s still in school, Leon. And there’s no way you could’ve arranged all the travel documents for my wife and child on such short notice. You’re the only person I know who suddenly decides we’re going on an overseas trip with barely any warning."
Leon scratched the back of his head after hearing that.
"I got trapped inside a domain, so there’s literally nothing else for me to do. Even when I log into the game, all I can do is sit there doing nothing. Do you know how depressing that is?"
"I do understand that. I’ve known you long enough while working for you."
"You get it," Leon said. "Good thing Freya handled all the arrangements and managed to put this trip together."
"Well, if your real intention was to take Freya on vacation, you didn’t really need to invite me. I’m pretty sure Freya alone would’ve been more than enough to keep you company."
Leon didn’t answer. He simply looked out the window as the car continued smoothly through the city streets.
Eventually, they arrived at the airport and made their way toward the departure lounge.
Once they entered the waiting area, they spotted two familiar figures sitting in the distance.
"Why are they sitting so far apart?" King asked.
"No idea. Maybe they just wanted some personal space," Leon replied.
"And why are Freya and Laura both here?" King asked again.
"They’re part of Vensalor too. Why wouldn’t they be?"

"If you’re taking your two girlfriends on vacation, then you definitely don’t need me tagging along," King replied. "Well... actually, I guess you do. I almost forgot I’m your bodyguard now. Fine, I’ll make sure the three of you have a great vacation while you spend time with those two."
"I think you’re reading way too much into this, King," Leon answered in his usual flat tone. "A vacation is a vacation. We’re all just traveling together."
As they got closer, Freya came into view first. She was sitting with one leg crossed over the other, wearing a pair of black sunglasses that contrasted with her brown hair.
Laura, on the other hand, was seated a short distance away. She wore a light-colored outfit, and her blonde hair fell in soft, gentle waves over her shoulders.
The moment she noticed Leon approaching, Laura immediately stood up and walked toward him as Leon and King made their way over as well.
"Leon," Laura said, smiling a little wider than usual. Maybe it only seemed that way because Leon had been staring at King’s stiff expression the entire drive over.
"I’m a little confused. Why did you tell me to come this early? Our flight isn’t for another three hours, right? Still, I’m glad I didn’t end up arriving late."
"Three hours?" Leon repeated, looking confused.
Freya lowered her sunglasses before standing up as well.
"Oh... about that. The flight we’re taking sold out just as I was booking the tickets, so Laura had to take the next flight instead."
Hearing that, Laura’s expression shifted ever so slightly. A moment later, though, she smiled again.
"Oh, that’s why. Okay then. We’ll just meet at our destination."
Leon turned toward Freya, though he didn’t say a word.
"What?" Freya asked. "You don’t actually think I did that on purpose, do you?"
"Of course not. Why are you reacting like that?"
"No, Leon, I really don’t mind," Laura said with a gentle smile. "I’m actually grateful you bought my ticket too. I’ll pay you back later."
"Exactly. You don’t have to pay for everything, Leon," Freya added. "You’re spoiling everyone."
Watching the conversation between the three of them, King could only let out a sigh.
"Maybe it’s actually for the best that Freya and Laura are on separate flights."
Unfortunately for him, he had said it out loud instead of keeping it to himself.
Both girls immediately turned to look at him.
"Not you too, okay, King?" Freya protested. "There’s nothing going on here. Stop jumping to the same conclusions as Leon."
"Why am I the one getting blamed now, huh?" Leon shot back.
After that, they waited together for a while until it was finally time for Leon, Freya, and King to board, while Laura stayed behind to wait for her next flight.

The flight itself was fairly long. Fortunately, they were seated in the premium cabin, so the journey never felt too tiring. Leon spent most of the flight asleep, having deliberately stayed awake the night before so he could rest during the trip instead.
After landing, the three of them continued on together as they entered the arrival hall, only to find that it was far more crowded than it should have been.
"Why are there so many people in black suits over there?" King asked.
As they walked closer, they could see an even larger crowd gathered ahead, with people raising their phones to take photos.
Eventually, the crowd parted, revealing who everyone had been surrounding.
"Heejin?" King said in surprise as the famous Korean artist with long black hair came into view.
"Heejin came too, Leon? Was that just a coincidence?" King asked again.
Freya smirked as she looked at him.
"You’d be surprised if you knew who he asked to come to Japan on such short notice."
King blinked.
"Don’t tell me... the entire guild?"
"What do you think?" Freya replied.
"So... is this actually a vacation, or is it work?" King asked again.
"If you really know Leon, that question shouldn’t even have crossed your mind."
"Okay, then."
King gave a small nod and simply kept walking. As they approached, they were finally allowed through the tightly guarded security circle formed by Heejin’s bodyguards.

chapters.title: Chapter 913 - The Loudest Whisper
paragraphs: From the moment they left the airport, throughout the drive to the hotel, even after they had checked in, and right up until the main gathering finally began that evening, King kept letting out sigh after sigh, shaking his head as though he still couldn’t believe any of this was real.

Leon now stood inside one of the hotel’s grand ballrooms. Crystal chandeliers hung from the high ceiling, while elegantly arranged round tables filled the spacious hall. Every detail, from the lighting to the decorations, reflected the luxury of the venue. And judging from their appearance alone, the guests gathered there were clearly not ordinary people.

Leon could only smile at the remark.
"Well, I just hope I don’t disappoint everyone’s expectations."
"I think you just got lucky," the black-haired woman behind Juliette suddenly cut in.
It was Forev, the archer and Juliette’s assistant.
"Yeah," Leon replied with a faint smile. "I really was just lucky. You’re not wrong about that."
Juliette let out a soft laugh.

"No matter how great someone’s luck is, it only matters if it falls into the hands of the right person. Luck alone isn’t enough. It still takes determination, hard work, talent, and the ability to make the most of every opportunity. None of this would’ve happened if it had been anyone other than Leon."
She glanced back at her assistant. "Forev, I think you could try being a little nicer to Leon whenever you meet him."
"I am nice to him. Even in the game."
Leon could only smile before excusing himself to continue greeting the other guests.
A moment later, a tall blond man stood up and strode confidently toward Leon with long, energetic steps. As soon as he reached him, he pulled Leon into a firm hug.

"My brother, my hero, my inspiration, my legend. Leon, the best. The GOAT," he declared before letting go with a wide grin. "I seriously feel honored to be here. Getting invited to something this special means a lot to me. I wouldn’t have missed it for anything."
"Glad you could make it too, Ronald."

"How could you even say that?" Ronald replied dramatically. "I’ll always be the first one to answer your call, and I’ll go beyond whatever you expect from me. If you told me to fly to the other side of the world right now, I’d already be on the plane."

"Tonight is going to be something special, isn’t it? I can feel it in the air." His grin widened even further. "I even brought several sponsors with me. They’re waiting outside right now. We’re going to bring in a lot of money. This is going to be huge.
Freya let out a long sigh.
"In the end, your mind always comes back to business, doesn’t it, Ron?"
Ronald paused and turned toward her with a serious look.
"You too, Freya."
"I think the same applies to you, Freya."
Ronald and King said it at exactly the same time.
"Yeah, you too, Freya," Leon said this time, turning to look at her.
"Not you too, Leon!" Freya protested. She reached over to pinch his side, but Leon casually stepped away and laughed.
"Wait... not here! We can have our pillow fight after we get home, okay?"
"Fine," Freya replied with a small nod. "I can hold myself back until then."
Hearing that, Ronald leaned toward King and whispered,
"So... they’re sleeping in the same bed now? And they even have pillow fights first?"
Unfortunately, his whisper was far louder than he intended. At that exact moment, the background music happened to pause between songs.
Everyone in the ballroom turned to look at Leon and Freya.
Leon immediately rubbed his forehead.
"I told you we shouldn’t have invited this brainless idiot," Freya muttered.

chapters.title: Chapter 914 - The Frozen Truth
paragraphs: Leon and Freya continued greeting the remaining guests until a server approached them carrying a polished display tray. Resting neatly on top were several sleek white visors. Their frames were smooth and minimal, while the dark lenses gave no hint of what lay behind them.
Leon casually picked one up, with Freya following a moment later.

"They’re the latest product released by Juliette’s company," Freya explained. "The Immortal Legacy Visor. This is the compact version. Instead of using a full immersion capsule, users can enter Immortal Legacy through this device alone. It’s far more flexible, portable, and can be used almost anywhere. Of course, some advanced functions are limited compared to the full capsule system."
Leon gave a small nod.
"You’ve finished all the preparations, haven’t you?"

"Everything is ready. Juliette and Ronald were a huge help throughout the process, and every required record has already been mapped and organized. We’ll be holding the meeting inside the Immortal Legacy environment tonight. That way, any eyes or ears that shouldn’t witness what you’re about to discuss will be kept far away from the conversation."
Leon nodded again.
The time had finally come.
He walked toward the center of the grand hall, noticing that the other guests were already holding their own visors in anticipation.
Waiting there for him was a chair unlike any other in the room. It was a high-backed reclining seat built from polished black alloy with subtle silver accents running along its frame.

When Leon arrived, he didn’t sit immediately. Instead, he remained standing as every conversation in the ballroom gradually faded away. One after another, the guests turned their attention toward him, each already wearing their visor and waiting for him to begin.
"Let us begin."
Leon slowly placed the visor over his eyes.
The lenses lit up with a soft blue glow.
An instant later, the world around them began to change.
The luxurious ballroom dissolved piece by piece as if reality itself were being repainted. Marble floors transformed into lush green grass stretching endlessly in every direction.
Towering ancient trees rose around the gathering, their branches spreading wide overhead before opening into a brilliant blue sky filled with drifting white clouds.

Elegant dining tables and refreshment stations still remained, yet they no longer looked like ordinary furniture. They blended seamlessly into the vast meadow, crafted from polished wood and living vines as though they had always belonged within this peaceful landscape.
It felt as if reality and fantasy had become one.
Leon looked around as every guest completed the synchronization.

One after another, they appeared in the avatars they used inside the game. Their faces remained the same, making it easy to recognize one another, but each person now wore the equipment they had last logged out with.
This wasn’t the live Immortal Legacy server.

Instead, it was an isolated simulation environment, a complete mirror of the game world created specifically for meetings and strategic planning. Everything from the terrain and buildings to combat data and character records had been faithfully replicated. Here, they could discuss important matters without worrying about outside surveillance, test their characters’ skills, spar with one another, or even enter training grounds filled with simulated monsters.
It was, in every sense, a private version of Immortal Legacy.
Compared to the prototype simulation system that had existed years ago, this upgraded environment was vastly more advanced, capable of recreating almost every aspect of the real game.
Leon now stood once again within Broken’s familiar body.
He glanced around before stopping at the sight behind him.
Kingsley stood there with his massive frame, looking as imposing as ever. Beside him was Freya, clad in her elegant silver armor, her long brown hair flowing gently behind her.
Leon stepped forward and looked at the countless members of Vensalor gathered before him.

"Welcome, everyone, to the grand gathering of Vensalor. Seeing all of you here today is something I never imagined would become reality. Every achievement we’ve reached, every battle we’ve won, and every challenge we’ve overcome was only possible because all of you stood together. So today isn’t about celebrating me. It’s about celebrating every single one of us. Thank you... for making Vensalor what it is today."
For a brief moment, silence filled the field.
Then the entire crowd erupted.

Thunderous applause echoed across the grasslands. Cheers rose from every direction as some members whistled, others shouted at the top of their lungs, and several even jumped into the air in excitement.
"Since when did Broken learn how to give speeches like that?" Jovine said.
"Freya definitely wrote that."
"Was he reading from a script or something?"
Melliandra folded her arms before turning her face away with a scoff.
"It was stiff. Way too rehearsed. Doesn’t fit Broken’s shameless face at all."
Not far away, RememberMe suddenly dropped to one knee.
"My King Broken... you’ve grown so much. I knew there was a reason I’d devoted myself to worshipping you from the very beginning!"
"Why is this idiot still here?" someone immediately complained.
"Can someone throw him out already?"
Laughter spread through the crowd.
At that very moment, a loud voice shouted from the opposite side of the gathering.

"Broken! You’re my best friend! I was your very first friend in this game, and I’m proud of that! Everyone else here is fake! They only became your friends after they realized how ridiculously strong you are!"
It was Booba.
Elincia shot him an icy glare as blue lightning crackled around her body.
"Can you just shut up?"
Broken simply smiled before clearing his throat.
"Well... to be honest, I spent quite a while thinking about that opening speech."
"Turns out, that kind of thing just doesn’t suit me. So... let’s skip the formalities and get straight to the main topic."
The crowd chuckled before quickly settling down again, their attention returning to him.
Broken’s expression gradually became serious.
"I’m in a pretty desperate situation right now," he said.
The smiles on everyone’s faces disappeared.
Before anyone could ask what he meant, the scenery around them suddenly shifted.
The vast meadow vanished in an instant.
The world itself seemed to move around them at incredible speed, while they remained standing exactly where they were.
Mountains, forests, rivers, and endless landscapes rushed past like a rapidly changing panorama, leaving many of them staring with wide eyes.
Moments later, everything came to an abrupt stop.
An icy wind slammed into them.
The clear blue sky had been replaced by dark, storm-filled clouds. Snow swirled violently through the air as a brutal blizzard raged in every direction.
In the blink of an eye, they found themselves standing in the heart of a merciless frozen wasteland.
